title: Move a child v-model to defineModel

files.content:
<script setup lang="ts">
const props = defineProps<{ modelValue: string }>()
</script>

<template>
  <input v-model="props.modelValue" type="search" placeholder="Search" />
</template>

summary: SearchBox writes to props.modelValue and gets a readonly warning. Wire it back to the parent with defineModel.

turns.user: typing in SearchBox logs Set operation on key "modelValue" failed: target is readonly. parent just does <SearchBox v-model="query" />

assistant.body: Got it. Props are read only from the child's side, so the v-model on the input tries to write to props.modelValue and gets refused. On Vue 3.4 or later, let's reach for defineModel. It folds receiving the prop and emitting update:modelValue into a single ref, which you hand straight to the input. Note: without required: true the type is string | undefined. The parent's v-model keeps working as it is.

<script setup lang="ts">
const model = defineModel<string>({ required: true })
</script>

<template>
  <input v-model="model" type="search" placeholder="Search" />
</template>

turns.user: oh wait, another repo is still on 3.3 so no defineModel there. how does that one look

assistant.body: Up to 3.3 you declare the prop and the emit yourself and wire them up. In other words, all defineModel does is bundle those two. Pass the value in with :value and emit update:modelValue on the input event. The flow is the same either way: the child never writes to props, it hands the new value to the parent and the parent writes it.

<script setup lang="ts">
defineProps<{ modelValue: string }>()

const emit = defineEmits<{
  'update:modelValue': [value: string]
}>()

function onInput(event: Event) {
  emit('update:modelValue', (event.target as HTMLInputElement).value)
}
</script>

<template>
  <input :value="modelValue" type="search" placeholder="Search" @input="onInput" />
</template>
